The 'closed-world bundle mode' product call (doc 13 §9) should only allow guard removal for facts the bundle can prove, as the doc 13 PROVEN rule already says.

When a fast layout depends on whole-program knowledge, put the fallback in the same data format, as Kotlin's GHA does with the sign bit of interfaceTableSize: fast perfect-hash itable, or binary search. ep9 shape and IC layouts chosen at AOT time (snapshot root ShapeIds, H35) should carry an in-band 'not the fast form' marker that the code tests, so a unit built without the closed-world pass still runs correctly.

Do not plan on whole-program AOT for release with per-unit caching for dev and nothing in between. Kotlin ended up with fast-but-weak debug builds and slow uncached release builds, and gives users no middle mode. For ep9, aim for optimized-AOT that is per-unit and guarded, with whole-program passes as an optional extra that never changes correctness. Then caching and optimization do not exclude each other.

Keep the tiering policy aware of compile-queue load, as HotSpot does: thresholds scale with queue length, and a method goes to a cheaper profiling tier when the top-tier queue is long, because level 2 is about 30% faster than level 3. For ep9 hybrid re-tier (H33: aot-opt, then instrumented T1, then T2), add a rule that the instrumented tier is skipped or shortened when the T2 queue is long. Make the 1,000-call re-tier number (est.) scale with load rather than stay fixed.

Training profiles must stay hints that runtime feedback overrides (JEP 515: cached profiles 'do not prevent additional profiling'). Do not try to minimize the interpreter: JEP 544 found that near-total AOT gives cache files that load slower than interpreting, and lower peak. This supports H33's precedence rule (RUNTIME > PROFILED > HINTED) and the A3 'unit text <= 8x bytecode' cap. Track the load time of the unit as a cost beside its size.

Plan for module init and constant facts in AOT code. JEP 544 cannot fold static finals and compiles a slow version (with init checks) and a fast version, switching at runtime. Kotlin/Native removes init checks by whole-program data flow and made globals lazy. In ep9 AOT code, TDZ and module-init checks and module-level const values need either two code versions or a fuse that patches the check once init is done. Do not bake init state into unit text.

GC choices baked into AOT code are part of the unit identity. jaotc needed four java.base builds (GC × compressed oops). JEP 544 still requires the same GC because barriers are in the code. Kotlin keys caches on -Xgc. ep9 H35's barrier version field is correct. Do not add a second GC with different barriers unless the unit format can hold both barrier forms or the loader drops to bytecode. Also take from Kotlin's MM rewrite: build a simple stop-the-world collector first as the oracle for 'did we find every root' (H10), before any concurrent collector.

On iOS (jitless plus a host ARC world), expect Kotlin's problems. Host objects held by the engine are freed only at GC, chains take one cycle per hop, mixed retain cycles leak, and finalizers must run on the main thread or a GC thread with a run loop. Build an external-refcount root registry (like ExternalRCRefRegistry), a background or app-state-aware GC scheduler, and a 'stable refs' counter in GC logs early. Avoid Kotlin's closed-world duplication trap: two separately built ep9 bundles in one app must not each own a copy of the same shapes or classes, or must be linked as one 'umbrella'.

Do not keep two code generators for one thing. Kotlin had a second LLVM generator for ObjC bridges and paid a sync cost until Swift export turned bridges into ordinary source for the one compiler. JVM jaotc (a second compiler, Graal) was removed for low use and high upkeep. Its replacement reuses C1/C2 output. In ep9, baseline-AOT and optimized-AOT must be the T1 and T2 compilers run ahead of time (the masm unit-finalize path), not a separate AOT compiler. Embedder and interop bridges should be generated as ordinary bytecode or IR.

Plan every replacement as a long overlap with a dated kill switch, and budget for it. Kotlin's MM went announce (2020), preview (2021), default (1.7.20), removal (1.9.20), and the K1 descriptor path still lives in Native ObjC export in 2026. JS legacy went deprecated (1.8.0), then error (1.9.0), with libraries shipping both formats meanwhile. When ep9 changes a frozen contract (H35 container, H2 bytecode ABI), ship the reader for the old version for one tagged period and test both, then delete it on a date set in the decision log.

Make ABI changes visible as text in CI. Kotlin's klib dump-abi writes one line per declaration and the line changes when the ABI breaks. Kotlin also states klib compatibility as one-way (old readable by new, never the reverse). For ep9, add a 'dump unit ABI' tool (header versions, section kinds, link-table and IC-cell layout) with golden files, and state the direction of compatibility in H35 for each field.

On wasm hosts, the host's GC and JIT are the engine's tiers. Kotlin/Wasm emits WasmGC structs and lets the browser do the rest, keeps a JS fallback build for old browsers, and is now moving from whole-program to per-module output for load-on-demand. If ep9 ever targets wasm as a host, the interpreter plus jitless AOT units are the whole engine. Keep the unit format per-module from the start rather than whole-program.

failures_and_reversals: Kotlin/Native legacy memory manager: deferred reference counting, a cycle collector and object freezing (2016). It was chosen 'for its simplicity' and its fit with ObjC ARC. It blocked shared concurrent code and leaked with AtomicReference cycles in multithreaded coroutines ('we don't have a clear solution'). Replaced by a tracing GC: roadmap Jul 2020, preview 2021, default 1.7.20, removed 1.9.20 (Nov 2023). Freezing is deprecated and always off. Side effects: global property init became lazy, and caches did not support the old MM during the overlap. Sources: JetBrains blog 2020-07 and 2021-05; kotlinlang whatsnew1720; native-migration-guide.

Kotlin/Native allocator: mimalloc replaced by a custom paged allocator, default in 1.9.20. The paged layout allows independent, consecutive sweeping (kotlinlang whatsnew1920; runtime/src/alloc/custom/README.md).

Kotlin/Native GC marking: partial parallel mark (a GC thread marks globals and native-state threads) was replaced in 1.9.20 by full parallel mark, because the old scheme 'is not the case for typical iOS applications' (whatsnew1920).

Kotlin/JS legacy backend (direct from the frontend to JS) replaced by the IR backend: IR Stable and legacy deprecated in 1.8.0, LEGACY/BOTH an error in 1.9.0. Users had to change code; libraries published 'joined' legacy+IR klibs during the overlap (ChangeLog-1.8.X KT-55593; ChangeLog-1.9.X KT-54452; js-ir-migration).
Kotlin/JVM old backend replaced by the JVM IR backend, default in Kotlin 1.5 (KT-44021). Debugger dependencies on K1 and the old JVM backend were removed in the 2.2 line (KT-70139).

K1 frontend replaced by K2/FIR (stable in 2.0, May 2024). The tail is not finished: Native ObjC framework export still runs a K1 frontend phase in 2026 (TopLevelPhases.kt:61-68; NativeCompilerDriver.kt:56-69). Language version 1.9 was dropped for non-JVM targets in 2.3 (KT-76344).

Klib inline semantics: klib backends inlined after linking (a dependency's new inline body won), unlike the JVM (body frozen at library compile time). The team chose the JVM model and is moving inlining before klib serialization (KT-64570). Old klibs stay on the late model as accepted tech debt (docs/inlining/klib-inining.md:1-40, 388-397).

Kotlin/Native library linkage: a linkage error used to fail the build. Since 1.9.0 the broken declaration becomes a run-time throw (JVM-like), and since 1.9.20 these issues are silent by default (whatsnew19, whatsnew1920).

ObjC export (2017, a second LLVM IR generator, tied to K1 descriptors, poor IDE fit) is being superseded by Swift export (started 2023, a separate tool generating Swift plus Kotlin bridges built by the normal compiler) (docs/swift-export/architecture.md).

JDK jaotc / Graal AOT (JEP 295, JDK 9: ELF libraries keyed by GC × compressed oops, tiered AOT that re-profiled at C1 Tier 3) was removed in JDK 17 (JEP 410): 'little use ... maintenance significant', and left out of Oracle JDK 16 builds with 'no one complained'. Replaced by Leyden: JEP 483 (JDK 24), 514 and 515 (JDK 25), 544 AOT code from C1/C2 in the AOT cache (JDK 28, Completed).

Leyden workflow changes: the two-step record/create was called 'cumbersome' in JEP 483 and given a one-step AOTCacheOutput in JEP 514. AOTMode=on was renamed AOTMode=required in JDK 27. JEP 483 did not support ZGC at first; JEP 544 lists ZGC among the supported GCs.

Leyden open item (JEP 544 future work): experiments with near-total AOT (minimal interpreter and JIT) gave cache files too large to load faster than interpreting, and lower peak. JEP 544 keeps 'AOT-only mode' a non-goal.

Kotlin/Wasm: whole-program output today; JetBrains (May 2025) is moving to per-module Wasm output for faster rebuilds and on-demand loading. A Compose 'compatibility mode' falls back to the JS build where WasmGC is missing.

Caveats on my own sources: blog.jetbrains.com and openjdk.org returned 403 to WebFetch, so I fetched them with curl and read the text. The Kotlin 2.2.20 Beta date (Sep 2025) comes from a search result, not a page I read. The kotlinlang js-ir-migration page is gone (404), so the rationale quote is from the w3cub mirror of the Kotlin 1.9 docs. Lowering counts (80/98/119/92) are grep counts, est. ±5. I read no number for Kotlin/Native vs JVM steady-state speed, so none is given.

system: Dart VM (dart-lang/sdk, HEAD 0f1a89e1, 2026-11-18): CFE -> Kernel -> one flow-graph compiler used as JIT (unoptimized + IC -> optimized + deopt) and AOT (TFA closed world, dispatch table, no deopt), app-jit/app-aot/module snapshots, plus the 2024+ bytecode interpreter for dynamic modules and an experimental 2026 modular AOT compiler written in Dart. Source clone: a sparse clone of dart-lang/sdk. Prefix 'sdk:' below means a path in that clone at 0f1a89e1.

findings.claim: Since Dart 2 the VM cannot run raw source. It takes only Kernel binaries (.dill) made by the shared CFE (written in Dart). The standalone 'dart' tool hosts CFE in a 'kernel service' isolate. Flutter runs CFE on the host (frontend_server) and ships Kernel to the device.
findings.mechanism: VM loads Kernel lazily: first only libraries/classes, class members on first use, and function bodies only when compiled. Each VM object keeps an offset back into the Kernel blob. Every function starts pointing to LazyCompileStub.

findings.topic: Kernel is version-locked, not a stable public format
findings.claim: The VM accepts only one exact Kernel binary format version, and it also checks an SDK hash. A .dill from another SDK build is rejected. 'Stable IR' holds only inside one SDK build.
findings.mechanism: kernel_binary.cc reads formatVersion and rejects it if it is not equal to kSupportedKernelFormatVersion, then runs IsValidSdkHash. The CFE side has BinaryFormatVersion with the comment 'Bump it when making incompatible changes'.
findings.numbers: kSupportedKernelFormatVersion = BinaryFormatVersion = 142 at 0f1a89e1

findings.topic: Whole-program facts travel as Kernel metadata
findings.claim: TFA runs in Dart, in gen_kernel. Its results reach the C++ VM as typed metadata repositories attached to Kernel nodes, not as a new IR.
findings.mechanism: pkg/vm/lib/metadata has inferred_type (flags: nullable, int, skipCheck, constant, receiverNotInt, closure, exactClass, exactType), direct_call, procedure_attributes (dynamic-call/tear-off/this-use bits plus selector ids packed into 64 bits), table_selector, unboxing_info, unreachable, loading_units, obfuscation_prohibitions and closure_id. The VM reads each one with its own MetadataHelper class. KernelLoader::ReadInferredType sets the field's guarded_cid and nullability from it.

findings.topic: One optimizing pipeline for JIT and AOT
findings.claim: JIT and AOT share one pass list (CompilerPass::RunPipeline). Mode differences are a few AOT-only pass calls plus a polymorphic CallSpecializer object.
findings.mechanism: INVOKE_PASS_AOT(X) expands to 'if (mode == kAOT) X' and exists only in DART_PRECOMPILER builds. AOT-only calls: ApplyClassIds and TypePropagation before the first ApplyICData, a second ApplyICData after ConstantPropagation, OptimizeTypedDataAccesses, DelayAllocations, and ApplyClassIds in the inlining pipeline. UseTableDispatch runs in both modes, but the base CallSpecializer::ReplaceInstanceCallsWithDispatchTableCalls is an empty virtual ('Only implemented for AOT'). AotCallSpecializer and JitCallSpecializer override the behavior.
findings.numbers: 6 AOT-only pass calls (5 in the main pipeline, 1 in the inlining pipeline). compiler/aot/*.cc + compiler/jit/*.cc = 7,709 lines (aot_call_specializer 1,320; jit_call_specializer 223; precompiler 4,088) out of about 261k non-test lines under runtime/vm/compiler (my wc).

findings.topic: Mode checks still spread through the compiler
findings.claim: Despite the shared pipeline, mode branches are spread through IL, codegen and stubs, many as per-instruction answers.
findings.mechanism: For example, several IL classes implement ComputeCanDeoptimizeAfterCall() as '!CompilerState::Current().is_aot()'. There are 23 mode mentions in il.h alone, and the stub compilers branch on FLAG_precompiled_mode for each architecture.
findings.numbers: Lines in runtime/vm/compiler: 202 with FLAG_precompiled_mode, 99 with is_aot(), 197 with DART_PRECOMPILED_RUNTIME. Across all of runtime/vm: 326 with FLAG_precompiled_mode and 1,312 with DART_PRECOMPILED_RUNTIME (grep line counts, my measurement)

findings.topic: AOT = the optimizing compiler with the speculation switches off
findings.claim: The AOT mode is set by a flag handler that turns off every feature that needs deopt or runtime recompilation.
findings.mechanism: PrecompilationModeHandler sets background_compilation=false, enable_mirrors=false, link_natives_lazily=true, optimization_counter_threshold=-1, polymorphic_with_deopt=false, precompiled_mode=true, use_field_guards=false, use_cha_deopt=false, and in non-product gen_snapshot also deoptimize_alot=false, deoptimize_every=0 and use_osr=false. AOT is not supported on IA32. The 2025 modular AOT handler flips the same set.

findings.claim: AOT pairs each speculative IL op with a non-speculative twin that throws or takes a slow path, so no guard ever deoptimizes.
findings.mechanism: CreateCheckBound picks GenericCheckBoundInstr in AOT (throws RangeError, or a 'phantom' when bounds checks are omitted by pragma). JIT gets CheckArrayBoundInstr, which deoptimizes. CheckNull throws. Polymorphic AOT call sites become PolymorphicInstanceCall 'without deoptimization' (cid checks, then a fallback call) when TFA/CHA cannot find one target. The intro doc says AOT code 'must not rely on any speculative assumptions' and its analyses 'err on the side of correctness'.

findings.topic: JIT pipeline: unoptimized code with ICs, then background optimization
findings.claim: The first compile is a fast one-to-many lowering of stack-style IL with inline-cache calls. Hot functions go to a background optimizing compiler, which builds SSA IL from the same Kernel and installs code at a safepoint.
findings.mechanism: ICData per call site holds (receiver class, target, count). A shared IC stub does a linear search and calls the runtime on a miss. On the threshold, OptimizeInvokedFunction enqueues the function to the BackgroundCompiler and sets the usage counter to INT32_MIN so it does not re-trigger. The caller keeps running the old code.

findings.claim: The optimization threshold scales with function size and is capped. Optimized code that still has ICs re-optimizes at a lower count. OSR triggers at loop stack checks, and deeper loops get higher thresholds.
findings.mechanism: Unoptimized threshold = min(optimization_counter_scale*basic_blocks + min_optimization_counter_threshold, optimization_counter_threshold). Optimized code uses reoptimization_counter_threshold. CheckStackOverflow in a loop increments Function::usage_counter and jumps to OSR when it reaches threshold*(loop_depth+1). System isolates always use the default.
findings.numbers: default cap 30,000. scale 2,000 per basic block, plus a 5,000 minimum. reoptimization 4,000. huge methods: 10,000 AST nodes or 200,000 bytes of unoptimized code disable optimizations (flag_list.h, object.cc:89-91)

findings.claim: Per-function deopt counters stop deopt loops: first inlining stops, then optimization is turned off for good.
findings.mechanism: When deoptimization_counter >= max_deoptimization_counter_threshold, the function is marked not optimizable and its counter is set to INT32_MIN. The inliner stops inlining after deoptimization_counter_inlining_threshold. Call sites with more than max_polymorphic_checks classes are treated as megamorphic.
findings.numbers: 16 deopts = no more optimization. 12 = no more inlining. 4 polymorphic checks (32 for equality). Inliner: depth 6, callee size 160, caller size 50,000, small leaf 50

findings.claim: Deopt works because optimized and unoptimized code are both built from the same Kernel by the same builder. Each instruction gets a deterministic deopt id that maps back to a point in unoptimized code.
findings.mechanism: Inline checks (CheckSmi, CheckClass) deopt eagerly. Global guards (CHA, field guards) discard dependent code when the world changes, which is lazy deopt. deopt_instructions.cc is a small interpreter that rebuilds the unoptimized frame. The VM usually throws away optimized code after a deopt and re-optimizes with new feedback. Because asserts change deopt ids, app-jit snapshots record asserts, field_guards and osr in their feature string.

findings.topic: Field guards (JIT) vs TFA field facts and unboxing (AOT)
findings.claim: JIT tracks each field's observed class id, nullability and list length, and invalidates code when a guard breaks. AOT turns field guards off, takes the field cid from TFA metadata instead, and unboxes fields only in precompiled mode.
findings.mechanism: ReadInferredType sets guarded_cid and is_nullable from TFA. With FLAG_precompiled_mode it sets is_unboxed for non-late, non-static, non-nullable fields of type double, int, or SIMD (when supported).

findings.claim: TFA is a whole-program analysis that 'Assumes strong mode and closed world'. It runs in gen_kernel after constant-based unreachable-code elimination, and it is on by default for AOT.
findings.mechanism: The steps are: RapidTypeAnalysis for the allocated classes (to converge faster), then TypeFlowAnalysis from main and the @pragma('vm:entry-point') roots, then TreeShaker (also write-only fields and protobuf shaking), TFADevirtualization, TableSelectorAssigner, SignatureShaker, UnboxingInfoManager and AnnotateKernel. Before TFA, VMConstantEvaluator folds platform consts (target OS, asserts, defines) so dead branches never reach TFA. With --no-tfa only a simple CHA devirtualization runs.

findings.claim: TFA stays tractable through explicit widening limits. It is global, not modular, and hard to parallelize.
findings.mechanism: TFAConfiguration widens to raw arguments once a selector has too many distinct invocations, uses wide cone types once there are too many allocated subtypes, and saturates an invocation after too many invalidations. A Sep 2020 issue to cut end-to-end AOT compile time led to TFA speedups and 'Approximate wide cone types' (Jan 2021). mraleph wrote that gen_snapshot could be parallelized (maybe at the cost of late tree shaking) but parallel TFA is an open problem.
findings.numbers: maxInterfaceInvocationsPerSelector 1000, largeSummarySize 300, maxDirectInvocationsPerSelector 10, maxAllocatedTypesInSetSpecialization 128, invalidationLimit 1000, maxCallStackDepth 500

findings.topic: Signature shaking and unboxing grouped by selector
findings.claim: AOT rewrites calling conventions for the whole program. Parameters that are never used or never passed are removed. Optional or named parameters that are always passed become required positional. Unboxed parameters and returns are chosen per dispatch-table selector, so every implementation behind one call site agrees on the ABI.
findings.mechanism: SignatureShaker groups instance methods by table selector id. A function is eligible only if it is never called with an unknown call signature. UnboxingInfoManager runs union-find over selector ids, joining each field's getter and setter, and unboxes 2-field records in return values.
findings.numbers: numRecordFieldsForReturnValueUnboxing = 2

findings.topic: Second tree shake inside the VM precompiler
findings.claim: After TFA, gen_snapshot runs its own reachability fixpoint over VM objects while compiling, then drops everything not retained. Size is cut twice: at Kernel level and at VM-object level.
findings.mechanism: Precompiler::DoCompileAll runs FinalizeAllClasses and SortClasses (cid ranges), PrecompileConstructors (for inlining size info), AddRoots/AddAnnotatedRoots, then Iterate (compile, add callees, selectors, fields to a fixpoint), AttachOptimizedTypeTestingStub, global object pool, FinalizeDispatchTable, ReplaceFunctionStaticCallEntries, Drop{Functions,Fields,Classes,Libraries,Metadata}, Obfuscate, DiscardCodeObjects, Dedup and PruneDictionaries. --write-retained-reasons-to explains why each object was kept.

findings.claim: Typed (non-dynamic) calls that cannot be devirtualized go through one row-displacement table indexed by class id plus a selector offset. It is compact because Dart 2's sound static types guarantee that a typed call never hits a hole, so holes need no noSuchMethod entries.
findings.mechanism: On x64 the call is 'movzx cid,[obj+15]; call [GDT + cid*8 + (selectorOffset-16)*8]', with GDT held in a reserved register biased by kOriginElement so small offsets fit a 1-byte displacement. DispatchTableGenerator's RowFitter interleaves selector rows into free slots (Driesen-Hölzle). TFA assigns selector ids. A Feb 2020 commit used TFA call counts to drop selectors with no reachable polymorphic call.
findings.numbers: kOriginElement: 16 (x64), 1023, 4096, 256 or 512 on other targets. Selector pruning: table -30% in dart2js, -49% in Flutter Gallery (312 KB less memory on ARM64), per the commit message

findings.claim: Calls on 'dynamic' receivers in AOT (and calls from JIT unoptimized code) use switchable calls. The runtime rewrites both the cache object and the stub target of the call site as it learns. They were first built for Dart 1 AOT, where every call used them.
findings.mechanism: States: Unlinked, then Monomorphic (direct call into a checked entry that tests the receiver cid), then SingleTarget (a cid-range test, which works because AOT and AppJIT training number classes depth-first), then linear ICData, then MegamorphicCache (hash) past a threshold. DRT_SwitchableCallMiss drives the transitions.

findings.claim: AOT dropped per-function Code/pool indirection. All code shares one global object pool, calls are pc-relative and patched at snapshot time, and PC-to-metadata lookup uses a sorted reverse table. The flag was added in Dec 2018 and is now the only mode (only comments still mention it).
findings.mechanism: There is one global object pool (GOP) in the object store, loaded into PP by the enter-Dart stub. Frames have no CODE_REG or PP slots. Static calls are relocated after precompilation. ReverseCodeTable / ReversePcLookupCache maps a PC to Code and CompressedStackMaps. Cost: a function's pool entries must commit into the GOP, and if that fails the precompiler recompiles the function. The code comment notes that two compiles of one method may give different IR 'due to instability of inlining heuristics'.
findings.numbers: est. (from a search summary of the Part 8 commit, not read): -3.7% RX on ARM, -1.4% on ARM64 in Flutter Gallery

findings.topic: Sound types and null safety as proofs
findings.claim: AOT relies on soundness. Dart 2.0 (2018-08-07) replaced unsound optional types and checked/production modes with one sound type system. Dart 3 (May 2023) requires sound null safety, and the VM dropped --no-sound-null-safety in 3.5.0 (2024-08-06). TFA, the dispatch table compression and signature shaking all assume soundness.
findings.mechanism: Signature shaking treats a parameter as 'checked' (needs a runtime check) only if it is covariant, or non-nullable while sound null safety is off. The dispatch table can skip noSuchMethod holes only because typed calls are sound (README:719). TFA's doc comment says it 'Assumes strong mode'.

findings.topic: JIT vs AOT performance per the Dart team
findings.claim: The team's position: 'Currently Dart VM JIT has best peak performance, while Dart VM AOT has best startup time'. AOT 'can't speculate'. The gap shrank between 2019 and 2022 but did not close.
findings.mechanism: JIT gets precise local types and a profile but pays for warmup. AOT proves properties globally but has no profile and cannot deopt. mraleph (2019): 'It is much easier to make a fast JIT for a language like Dart than a fast AOT'. In 2022 he said the remaining fixes 'will not help to fully close the gap'.
findings.numbers: Image package, 2019: JIT 1262 ms vs AOT 2084 ms (reporter). 2022, Dart 2.17-dev linux_x64: AOT 5822 ms vs JIT 5203 ms (about 11%). With Uint8List: 5682 ms (about 9%)

findings.claim: One snapshot mechanism covers four kinds: core heap only, heap + JIT code, heap + AOT code, and module snapshots. AOT code is mapped in place and becomes part of the heap without deserialization.
findings.mechanism: Snapshot::Kind is {kFull, kFullJIT, kFullAOT, kModule}, with magic 0xdcdcf5f5. The format is clustered serialization (after the Fuel/Parcels papers): a list of objects to make and how to link them. AOT code was added when the AOT compiler arrived, so the VM could run where JIT is impossible.

findings.claim: A snapshot loads only into the exact VM build and configuration that wrote it. There are no compatibility shims: a mismatch gives a clear 'Wrong full snapshot version' error.
findings.mechanism: Version::SnapshotString() is an md5 over the text of 15 VM source files (app_snapshot, dart, dart_api_impl, datastream, image_snapshot, object, raw_object, snapshot, symbols). The reader also checks a features string: build mode, sanitizers, shared_data, (JIT only) asserts, field guards, osr, coverage, plus code_comments, dwarf_stack_traces, arch and OS. OS must match exactly so that Platform.isAndroid etc. can be compile-time constants.
findings.numbers: 15 hashed files

findings.claim: AppJIT is Dart's hybrid: a training run, then the generated JIT code and VM data are serialized. At run time the VM can still JIT and deopt if the real profile differs. It was made for dartanalyzer and dart2js, which spent as much time JIT-compiling as working on small inputs.
findings.mechanism: 'dart --snapshot-kind=app-jit --snapshot=x'. The kFullJIT snapshot carries code compiled under speculation, so the deopt-relevant flags are part of the feature key (F23). Depth-first cid numbering is also done during AppJIT training, for the cid-range checks.

findings.topic: AOT output formats and iOS linking
findings.claim: gen_snapshot writes AOT as assembly (to be assembled into a static or shared library by the embedder, the iOS path), ELF, Mach-O dylib, or PE/COFF .obj. Flutter switched iOS to direct Mach-O in 2025, reverted, and relanded.
findings.mechanism: Dart_AotBinaryFormat {Elf=0, Assembly=1, MachO_Dylib=2, PECoff_Obj=3}. The symbols are _kDartSnapshotData/Text/Bss/BuildId. Assembly output 'should be compiled as a static or shared library and linked or loaded by the embedder'. Flutter PR #171626 (opened 2025-07-04, merged 2025-08-21) dropped the assembler step. It was reverted 2025-08-25 for an app-size regression (DWARF kept in the snapshot) and relanded as #174870 on 2025-12-02.

findings.claim: Deferred imports are split after whole-program compilation into loading units, each written as its own ELF shared object. In Flutter this works only on Android (AAB feature modules) and web. The whole app must still be built and uploaded at once.
findings.mechanism: Dart_CreateAppAOTSnapshotAsElfs takes a next-unit callback. The loading_units metadata comes from the deferred_loading transformation. Calls across units go through Code objects that the precompiler cannot discard. Flutter debug mode treats deferred imports as normal imports.

findings.claim: Size work is backed by attribution tools and by moving metadata out of the binary.
findings.mechanism: --print-instructions-sizes-to writes per-function sizes, and 'snapshot_analysis treemap/compare' shows them. --dwarf-stack-traces swaps in-snapshot CodeSourceMaps for DWARF that --strip removes and --save-debugging-info keeps aside (DWARF is not obfuscated). --obfuscate runs in Precompiler::Obfuscate, and vm:keep-name keeps a name. An -O1/-O2/-O3 design (optimization_levels.md) states the cost: 'Two additional code paths through compiler, increases the size of all testing matrices'.

findings.claim: Hot reload exists only in non-product JIT builds. Its semantics are late binding: methods are immutable atoms, method dictionaries are swapped, and fields keep their values.
findings.mechanism: isolate_reload.cc and object_reload.cc are compiled only under !PRODUCT && !DART_PRECOMPILED_RUNTIME. A reload clears inline caches and 'unfolds' inlining. Closures and stack frames keep their old function. Unboxed fields are boxed again during reload (MarkFieldBoxedDuringReload updates the GC bitmap). The new code comes as incremental Kernel from frontend_server.

findings.topic: iOS JIT dependence of debug mode
findings.claim: Flutter debug builds on iOS depend on a JIT loophole. iOS 18.4 beta (Feb 2025) closed it ('The app itself can no longer write into its own executable memory'). The team considered going back to an interpreter, then shipped an lldb-based workaround in Jul 2025. Apple said the restriction 'will be making a come back'.
findings.mechanism: Writes redirected through debugserver had a 200 ms baseline latency for any size from 1 B to 64 KB, too slow for a JIT. The fix does one write through debugserver and then flips mprotect. Options in dart-lang/sdk#60202 were simarm64 or reviving DBC. mraleph: 'Bytecode tailored to Dart is faster to interpret (and faster to generate)'.
findings.numbers: 200 ms per debugserver write

findings.claim: Dart has added and removed interpreters twice. DBC (2016) was a 'simulator' architecture, unoptimized code only, and early Flutter used it for iOS development builds. KBC (Kernel bytecode, first commit 2018-05-09) became a second JIT input format. It was never on by default, and bytecode in core libraries was turned off in Mar 2019 because the bytecode pipeline lacked optimizations the AST pipeline had. 'Remove bytecode mode from the VM' landed 2020-10-28. That commit gives no reason.
findings.mechanism: KBC in 2019: the core snapshot could carry bytecode, the JIT compiled from bytecode, and the interpreter stayed behind --enable-interpreter (commit 7b50b7a8, 2019-06-26). That meant two front ends into IL (AST->IL and bytecode->IL). Today compiler/frontend has only the Kernel->IL builders.
sources: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/163984 (mraleph: 'like we did in the early days of Flutter')
findings.numbers: The reason for the removal is not stated in the commit. That maintaining two IL front ends was the cost is my inference.

findings.topic: New interpreter (2024+) for dynamic modules: a terminal tier
findings.claim: A new bytecode interpreter (copyright 2024) runs dart2bytecode output inside both the AOT and JIT runtimes. It is a build-time opt-in (DART_DYNAMIC_MODULES), not shipped by default, because of its code-size cost. Bytecode functions are never compiled.
findings.mechanism: An interpreted Function's code slot holds the InterpretCall stub (Function::IsInterpreted compares against it), so compiled callers use the normal call path. CompileFunctionHelper asserts !is_declared_in_bytecode. The interpreter calls compiled code through the InvokeDartCodeFromBytecode stub under a setjmp buffer, on a separate interpreter stack ('TODO: Once we share the same stack, try to invoke directly'). Dynamic dispatch uses a 1024-entry LookupCache keyed by (cid, name, args descriptor). The file format is 'DBC3' version 4, with a section table and a deduplicated object table.
findings.numbers: interpreter.cc 5,023 lines. bytecode_reader.cc 3,272 lines. LookupCache 1,024 entries

findings.topic: Dynamic modules: a declared hole in the closed world
findings.claim: To load code after the AOT build, the host declares a 'dynamic interface' (callable, dynamically-callable, extendable, can-be-overridden, can-be-used-as-type). TFA keeps those parts open, so less is tree-shaken and fewer calls are specialized. Modules may only add code, never replace it. Loading is allowed only with the same app code, interface and SDK tools. There is no sandbox.
findings.mechanism: dynamic_interface_annotator turns the YAML into dyn-module:* pragmas before TFA. In TFA, receivers whose class hasDynamicallyExtendableSubtypes get an unknown target. Dynamic calls from modules are checked at run time against dynamically-callable. Not done yet: provenance validation, whole-program validation of dynamic calls, JIT runtime checks, FFI from modules.

findings.topic: Modular AOT and a new Dart-written native compiler (2025-2026, experimental)
findings.claim: The repo has an experimental 'modular AOT' path. It is ARM64-only, compiles modules to a module snapshot (kModule, format version 1, predefined clusters) that the VM loads in modular_aot_mode, and its compiler pkg/native_compiler (2026) is written in Dart on a new CFG/SSA IR (pkg/cfg) that dart2wasm also imports.
findings.mechanism: ModularAOTModeHandler: fatal on non-ARM64. It turns off field guards, CHA deopt, OSR and background compilation, and sets the counter to -1. native_compiler has an arm64 back end, register allocator, lowering, unboxing and a Mach-O image writer. Its README says experimental and maybe removed. Its purpose is not documented in the repo. The Mach-O, ARM64-only shape suggests iOS development without a JIT (my inference).

findings.claim: Kernel plus the shared transformations feed several back ends: the VM JIT/AOT, dart2wasm (WasmGC), dart2js and DDC (an incremental JS dev compiler). dart2wasm reuses the same TFA and has its own static and dynamic dispatch tables.
findings.mechanism: dart2wasm compile.dart calls globalTypeFlow.transformComponent. dart2wasm/lib has dispatch_table.dart, static_dispatch_table.dart and dynamic_dispatch_table.dart. dart.dev lists an incremental JS dev compiler, an optimizing JS compiler and an optimizing WasmGC compiler.

findings.claim: The VM's own doc says the JIT 'keeps to its Dart 1 roots and largely ignores statically typed nature of Dart 2'. It uses ICs and speculative devirtualization, not TFA or the dispatch table. So JIT and AOT reach the same code by different routes.
findings.mechanism: In JIT, call sites not yet executed stay as ICs for re-optimization, and megamorphic ones use megamorphic dispatch. guess_icdata_cid makes up feedback for arithmetic. In AOT, devirtualization is only by proof.

findings.claim: A Dart-on-LLVM AOT prototype (on the Dartino runtime) performed 'on a par with our more mature DartVM-based ahead-of-time solution', while 'The JIT is still a long way ahead'. No decision to adopt it was made.
findings.mechanism: GC needed statepoints, which 'inhibits a lot of optimizations'. Registers are spilled before each call so the GC can move them, and there are no callee-saved GC values. Stack-overflow and interrupt checks were missing (guessed to cost about 10%).
findings.numbers: about 90% of Dartino tests passed. est. 10% cost for the missing checks (author's guess)

findings.topic: GC interaction: unboxed fields and compressed pointers
findings.claim: Unboxed fields are recorded per class in a 64-bit UnboxedFieldBitmap that the GC reads, so only the first 64 words of an object can hold raw data. If the bitmap overflows, the field stays boxed. Compressed pointers cut heap use by 20-30% (not 50%).
findings.mechanism: Class layout sets the bitmap bits for raw words, or calls set_is_unboxed(false) when the offset is past the bitmap. Reload re-boxes the field and updates the bitmap. Compressed pointers keep the heap in a 4 GB aligned region and decompress by adding the heap base, so Smi ops must be 32-bit.
findings.numbers: 64-word bitmap limit. 20-30% heap reduction

findings.topic: Entry points must be declared, and are checked in JIT too
findings.claim: In AOT, anything reached from native or embedder code must carry @pragma('vm:entry-point'), or TFA and tree shaking break it. To narrow the JIT/AOT gap, the JIT checks these annotations too (except for mirrors and VM-service debugging).
findings.mechanism: AddAnnotatedRoots seeds the precompiler, and TFA adds the pragma'd members as roots. The same annotations tell obfuscation which names to keep.

findings.claim: User-facing AOT tooling also changed. The standalone dart2native tool was removed in Dart 2.15.0 (2021-12-08) in favor of 'dart compile exe' and 'dart compile aot-snapshot'. The AOT runtime is a cut-down JIT runtime without the compiler.
findings.mechanism: The precompiled runtime (DART_PRECOMPILED_RUNTIME) 'does not contain any compiler components and is incapable of loading Dart source code dynamically'. So the AOT runtime has no re-tier path at all, except the opt-in interpreter.

lessons.lesson: Keep one front end and one serialized program form (like Kernel), but treat it as version-locked inside one engine build: exact version number plus a build hash, with a clean refusal on mismatch. Do not promise a stable public bytecode. Pass whole-program and TS-hint results as separate, tagged side metadata keyed to IR nodes (as Dart's inferred_type, direct_call and unboxing_info repositories are), so consumers ignore what they do not know and the IR itself never grows analysis fields.

One optimizing pipeline for JIT and AOT works (Dart has 6 AOT-only pass calls), but mode checks spread unless you forbid them: Dart has about 300 mode branches across its compiler. ep9's rule that passes read guard policy as data, never the mode, is stricter than Dart and worth enforcing with a lint. Two concrete shapes to copy: a policy object (CallSpecializer subclasses, empty virtual for 'not in this mode'), and paired IL ops (deopting CheckArrayBound vs throwing GenericCheckBound) chosen in one factory function.

Copy Dart's explicit per-function tiering state: a size-scaled threshold (2000 per block + 5000, capped at 30000), a lower re-optimization threshold for optimized code that still has ICs (4000), an OSR threshold scaled by loop depth, background compile that resets the counter to INT32_MIN while queued, and hard give-up counters (12 deopts: no inlining, 16: never optimize again). These numbers are tuned for Dart. ep9 should treat them as starting values, but the give-up structure is essential.

Deopt is simple in Dart because both tiers are built by the same deterministic builder from the same IR, and every speculative instruction carries a deopt id that maps to unoptimized code. ep9 should keep the T0 bytecode pc as the only deopt target and keep IR building deterministic. Any flag that changes the id mapping (Dart: asserts) must go into the code-cache or snapshot key. Dart's global guards (field guards, CHA) are ep9's fuses, and in AOT Dart replaces them with TFA facts rather than guards.

AOT without deopt is viable but leaves a real peak gap on code that is polymorphic in practice (Dart: 9-11% in 2022, up to 80% in 2019 cases). Dart closes part of the gap with proofs (TFA), a dispatch table and switchable calls, and never re-tiers, because its AOT runtime has no compiler. ep9's hybrid re-tier is exactly what Dart lacks. Keep it as the planned answer for peak, and keep jitless mode on SLOWPATH/PIN, like Dart's throwing checks.

A closed world pays off a lot (dispatch table -49% after selector pruning, signature shaking, unboxing grouped by selector), but every escape needs an explicit declaration (vm:entry-point, and years later the dynamic-interface YAML). For JS, closed-world facts should hold only inside one AOT unit with a declared interface. Plan the 'open hole' marker (Dart's hasDynamicallyExtendableSubtypes) from day one, not as a retrofit. Also budget compile time: TFA is global and hard to parallelize, so give the analysis explicit widening limits like TFAConfiguration.

Dart's compatibility key is blunt and safe: an md5 over the sources that affect the format, plus a features string (build mode, compile-affecting flags, arch, OS, sanitizers), checked on load with a readable error. ep9's H35 header should carry an equivalent features string, built from one macro list of flags so it cannot drift. Dart's 2024-2026 module formats (bytecode 'DBC3' v4, module snapshot v1) carry their own version numbers separate from the main snapshot. Their trust model is 'same app, same interface, same tools', which matches ep9's trusted-unit stance.

For startup, map AOT code and read-only data in place (no deserialization) and use clustered serialization for the heap part. AppJIT (training run, then serialize JIT code plus ICs, then keep JITting at run time) is the closest Dart analogue to ep9's hybrid warm start. Snapshot code that can deopt must carry its deopt metadata and the deopt-relevant flags. Number shapes/classes in a stable depth-first order at build time so range checks (Dart's SingleTarget cid ranges) work in snapshot code.

Build size tooling before size work: per-function size JSON plus treemap and compare tools, a 'retained reasons' dump, and DWARF line info that can be stripped and kept aside. Dart's biggest wins came from whole-program facts (selector pruning, signature shaking) and from removing per-function indirection (bare instructions: one global pool, pc-relative calls). The 2025 Mach-O revert for a size regression shows why size must be a CI gate, not a report.

Treat iOS as jitless for all builds, including dev. Flutter's debug JIT on iOS lived on a debugger loophole that Apple closed in iOS 18.4 beta, then partly kept via lldb, and Apple says the restriction is coming back. Ship AOT as linkable object or assembly output (Dart emits assembly, ELF, Mach-O dylib and PE/COFF), so the signed-app path never needs runtime code writes. Dart's experimental ARM64-only modular AOT compiler that writes Mach-O suggests they are moving the same way.

Dart removed its interpreter in 2020 and had to add one back in 2024 (dynamic modules) and again consider one in 2025 (iOS dev). This supports ep9's always-linked interpreter. But do not copy Dart's terminal-tier design (bytecode functions never compiled, a separate interpreter stack, setjmp at every interpreter-to-compiled call). Design shared frames and a uniform per-function entry slot from the start. Dart got the entry slot right: the InterpretCall stub sits in the Function code slot, so callers do not care.

Raw (unboxed) slots need GC metadata per layout, and Dart's fixed 64-word bitmap shows the trap of a fixed cap. Every layout-changing event (Dart: hot reload) must re-box or rewrite those slots and update the map. For ep9, put raw-slot info in shape side metadata with no hard word cap, and make debugger, reload and shape transitions handle unboxed fields explicitly.

Keep JIT and AOT behavior close by checking AOT-only contracts in JIT too (Dart checks vm:entry-point in JIT). Ship stress flags in the engine: deoptimize every N checks, deoptimize on every runtime call, threshold 1, stress background compilation. Count every new optimization level or mode as another test-matrix dimension, as Dart's -O design admits. ep9's mode x tier differential is the right gate.

Each extra execution format multiplied Dart's maintenance: DBC (2016), KBC as a second IL front end (2018-2020, never default, core libraries switched off over missing optimizations), the LLVM experiment (2017), the new interpreter (2024), and a Dart-written native compiler on a new CFG IR (2026). Cap ep9 to one bytecode and one IR. Require any second IL entry point to match all optimizations from day one, or not exist.

Soundness is what makes Dart's AOT cheap. The dispatch table has no holes and checks can be dropped only because Dart 2 and Dart 3 removed unsound modes. TS types are unsound, so ep9 cannot get Dart's dispatch-table compression or check removal from TS hints. A Dart-style vtable-like table for JS needs a selector-mismatch check in the method prologue (the Smalltalk variant the Dart doc mentions), or it must be limited to PROVEN sites.

failures_and_reversals: Dart 1 unsound optional types with separate 'checked' and 'production' modes were replaced in Dart 2.0 (2018-08-07) by one sound type system. Checked mode was removed (CHANGELOG 2.0.0).
Unsound null safety: optional from Dart 2.12, required by Dart 3 (May 2023). The VM removed --no-sound-null-safety in 3.5.0 (2024-08-06).

DBC interpreter / 'simulator' architecture (2016, unoptimized only) was used for early Flutter iOS dev builds, then dropped. I did not find the exact removal commit. mraleph in 2025: 'fallback to interpretation for development builds like we did in the early days of Flutter'.

KBC (Kernel bytecode): first commit 2018-05-09. The JIT could run from bytecode by 2019-06, but the interpreter stayed off by default. Core-library bytecode was switched off 2019-03-25 because the bytecode pipeline lacked optimizations. 'Remove bytecode mode from the VM' landed 2020-10-28 (7588ed86) with no stated reason.

Interpreter reversal: after the 2020 removal, a new KBC-style interpreter was added in 2024 for dynamic modules (opt-in build flag, not in the SDK by default). Reviving interpretation for iOS debug was considered in Feb 2025 (dart-lang/sdk#60202).

iOS JIT: Flutter debug JIT broke on the iOS 18.4 beta (2025-02). It was fixed with an lldb workaround on master (2025-07). Apple said the restriction 'will be making a come back'. dart-lang/sdk#60202 was still open in Nov 2025.
Dart 1 AOT compiled every call as a switchable call. Dart 2 AOT moved typed calls to a global dispatch table and kept switchable calls only for dynamic receivers.

The --use-bare-instructions flag (Dec 2018) went from optional to the only mode. Its cost: object-pool commit failures force recompiles, and the code notes inlining heuristics are unstable between compiles.
LLVM AOT back end prototype (Jan 2017) matched VM AOT but was not adopted ('no decision'). GC statepoints blocked optimizations.
AOT peak gap: 2019 reports of AOT up to about 80% slower than JIT (image package). By 2022 about 9-11%. mraleph: the remaining fixes 'will not help to fully close the gap'.
Flutter direct Mach-O output (PR #171626) merged 2025-08-21, reverted 2025-08-25 for an app-size regression (DWARF kept in the snapshot), relanded 2025-12-02 (#174870).
The standalone dart2native tool was removed in Dart 2.15.0 (2021-12-08) in favor of 'dart compile exe' / 'aot-snapshot'.
Dynamic modules (2024+) were still incomplete in Nov 2026: no provenance validation, no whole-program validation of dynamic calls, no JIT runtime checks, no FFI from modules. Not shipped in the SDK.
AOT compile time became a problem for large apps (issue #43299, Sep 2020). TFA was sped up (2020-2021), but TFA stays global and is not parallelized.

Sources: vm/jitinterface.cpp:13540-13548, inc/corjitflags.h:43, readytorun.h R2R 26.1 (StoreMultiCallableAddrOfCode, used on wasm).

R2R can carry PGO data and hot/cold splits. PgoInstrumentationData (section 117, v5.2+) embeds profile data in the image. HotColdMap (section 120, v8.0+) lets crossgen2 split methods into hot and cold parts. Sources: docs/design/coreclr/botr/readytorun-format.md:191-194, 776, 815-816.

Promotion bypasses and exclusions. [AggressiveOptimization] methods skip Tier0, instrumentation and PGO and go straight to Tier1 with no profile. Methods that MethodDesc::IsEligibleForTieredCompilation rejects work as if tiering were off. Sources: docs/design/features/DynamicPgo-InstrumentedTiers.md:11-13 (mermaid), tiered-compilation.md:84.

Separate code heap for optimized code. By default (SeparateOptimizedCodeHeaps=1), non-instrumented Tier1 and Tier1-OSR code in the global loader allocator go to their own code heap, apart from Tier0, instrumented, LCG and interpreter code. This keeps hot steady-state code together. Source: inc/clrconfigvalues.h:533-536.

Entry-point slot backpatching. By default (BackpatchEntryPointSlots=1), when a method's active code version changes, the runtime patches vtable and other entry-point slots directly instead of sending virtual calls through a precode. That is why virtual methods need the call-counting forwarder precode (F07). Sources: inc/clrconfigvalues.h:539-542, code-versioning.md:305, vm/callcounting.h:22-26.

MulticoreJit, an older startup mechanism alongside tiering. It records which methods were jitted at startup to a profile file and replays the JIT on a background thread in later runs (needs >= 2 CPUs). Sources: vm/multicorejit.cpp, multicorejitplayer.cpp; inc/clrconfigvalues.h:334-337; tiered-compilation.md:43 (lists MulticoreJit as a prior precompilation technique).

OSR transition details the finding left out. The OSR helper resets the frame counter to OSR_CounterBump on every call, even for invalid patchpoints, so other patchpoints in the method are not locked out. A CAS on patchpoint_triggered makes sure only one thread builds the OSR method; others keep running Tier0. Debug builds can filter patchpoints by id (OSR_LowId/HighId). Source: vm/jithelpers.cpp:1186-1300.

Mono's mibc use is method selection only. Mono profiled AOT (.NET 7) uses the .mibc only to choose which methods to AOT. It does not pass counts or class profiles to codegen. CoreCLR crossgen2 consumes the same .mibc for codegen and layout. Source: docs/design/mono/profiled-aot.md:5-30.

missed: Exceptions differ by mode. AOT has no deopt metadata: the environments of instructions that can throw become compressed CatchEntryMoves, a list of moves (constant from pool, tagged move, box an untagged value) that the runtime runs to build the catch-entry frame. JIT converts the lazy-deopt environment into CatchEntryMoves when an exception is caught. IL has no exception edges: each CatchBlockEntry acts like a separate function entry with Parameter instructions. Source: runtime/docs/compiler/exceptions.md:6-80

Type testing stubs (TTS). AssertAssignable calls a per-type stub that falls back to SubtypeTestCache and then the runtime. In AOT the precompiler guesses which types need a TTS (AttachOptimizedTypeTestingStub) and uses depth-first cid ranges. In JIT a TTS starts as LazySpecializeTypeTest, is rebuilt when more classes load, and is reset after hot reload. Source: runtime/docs/compiler/type_testing_stubs.md:1-85; precompiler.cc DoCompileAll (AttachOptimizedTypeTestingStub)

Field unboxing also happens in JIT from declared static types: Field::New calls UnboxFieldIfSupported for non-nullable, non-late instance fields of type double or SIMD. AOT adds TFA-proved int fields. Source: runtime/vm/object.cc:12459-12477; runtime/vm/compiler/runtime_api.cc:1054-1088

Checked vs unchecked entry points. TFA's flagSkipCheck in inferred-type metadata lets a call use a function's unchecked entry, which skips covariant parameter checks.
